locations.vanilla_source_en:
Seems like just yesterday I was pulled into this exciting new organization -- Constellation! We would push the boundaries of human knowledge and experience by exploring farther into space than anyone had before. "For all, into the Starfield." God, I was so young. We all were, but I was the youngest of us all. 

Now here we are, on the brink of disaster. The Colony War may be over, but the Settled Systems seems to just be waiting for the next one. Exploration is now, at best, "quaint," at worst, "irrelevant." Fortunately -- and it was no small feat -- I've managed to put together a list of potential new members. 

They are: 

Ervin Madani - young biologist and physician from the Freestar Collective. 

Barrett - promising young physicist from the UC (a "colorful" character to say the least...) 

Alice Campbell - "woman-of-action" and pilot, claims to have flown every type of ship at least once 

Russell Luther - astronomer and former Freestar Collective military (argumentative by effective) 

Visola Chen - philosopher, historian, specializes in humanity's early days of space exploration 

Jintao Min -- dedicated to finding "truth" among the stars (Neon hitman rumors are... troubling) 

With any luck, this "new blood" will be just what Constellation needs to keep going. Maybe. Hopefully. 

[From the personal diary of Aja Mamasa, former Constellation chair.]

items.source_en:
By Veris Hydan, Scholar of the Empire

Volume 1
History is a graveyard of forgotten truths. The foolish scribes of lesser civilizations record only what they wish to endure, shaping reality to their needs, erasing inconvenient wisdom, and leaving behind a hollowed-out husk of knowledge. But in the Ministry of Antiquity, we know better. We know that history is not what was written—it is what was hidden.

Look to the ruins of fallen worlds, to the shattered remains of once-mighty civilizations. If you believe their destruction was the result of chance, war, or mere misfortune, then you are already lost. Civilizations do not simply collapse—they are unmade. Something greater than them deemed their knowledge too dangerous to persist. And yet, the echoes of their truths remain, buried beneath dust, waiting to be uncovered.

It is said that there are places in this galaxy that hold knowledge beyond mortal comprehension. Great vaults of forgotten wisdom, temples built in reverence to powers long since stripped from the pages of history. I have seen such places. I have walked their halls and traced my hands over inscriptions worn by time. The symbols whisper of things that should not be spoken aloud, of understandings that cost entire species their existence.

But where others see danger, I see duty. We, the Ministry of Antiquity, are the caretakers of what should not be known. Ours is a burden of preservation—not for the masses, who would squander and misuse such knowledge, but for those with the wisdom to wield it.

[The first volume of Veris Hydan’s codex was widely circulated among Imperial scholars, though it was restricted from general access. Even among the learned, there are some things the Empire deems best left undiscovered.]
items.legacy_ko:
제국 학자, 베리스 하이단 저

제1권
역사는 잊힌 진실의 무덤입니다. 하급 문명의 어리석은 서기들은 자신들이 남기고 싶은 것만을 기록하며 필요에 따라 현실을 왜곡하고, 불편한 지혜를 지워버려 지식의 껍데기만을 남깁니다. 하지만 고대 유물부에서는 다르게 알고 있습니다. 우리는 역사가 기록된 것이 아니라, 숨겨진 것임을 알고 있습니다.

몰락한 세계의 폐허와 한때 강력했던 문명의 부서진 잔해를 보십시오. 그 파멸이 우연이나 전쟁, 혹은 단순한 불운의 결과라고 믿는다면 당신은 이미 길을 잃은 것입니다. 문명은 단순히 붕괴하지 않습니다. 그것은 해체되는 것입니다. 그들보다 위대한 무언가가 그들의 지식이 지속되기에는 너무 위험하다고 판단한 것입니다. 그럼에도 불구하고 진실의 메아리는 먼지 아래 묻힌 채 발견되기를 기다리고 있습니다.

이 은하계에는 필멸자의 이해를 넘어서는 지식을 간직한 장소들이 있다고 합니다. 잊힌 지혜의 거대한 금고와 역사책에서 오래전에 지워진 힘을 숭배하기 위해 세워진 사원들이 있습니다. 나는 그런 장소들을 보았습니다. 나는 그 홀을 걸었고 세월에 닳아버린 비문을 손으로 더듬었습니다. 그 상징들은 입 밖으로 내어서는 안 될 것들과 종족 전체의 존재를 대가로 치러야 했던 깨달음에 대해 속삭입니다.

하지만 다른 이들이 위험을 볼 때, 나는 의무를 봅니다. 우리 고대 유물부는 알려져서는 안 될 것들의 관리자입니다. 우리의 짐은 보존의 짐입니다. 그런 지식을 낭비하고 오용할 대중을 위해서가 아니라, 그것을 휘두를 지혜를 가진 자들을 위해서 말입니다.

[베리스 하이단의 코덱스 제1권은 제국 학자들 사이에서 널리 유통되었으나 일반적인 접근은 제한되었습니다. 학식 있는 자들 사이에서도 제국이 발견되지 않는 편이 낫다고 판단하는 것들이 있습니다.]

이 은하계에는 필멸자의 이해를 넘어서는 지식을 간직한 장소들이 있다고 합니다. 잊힌 지혜의 거대한 금고와 역사책에서 오래전에 지워진 힘을 숭배하기 위해 세워진 사원들이 있습니다. 나는 그런 장소들을 보았습니다. 나는 그 홀을 걸었고 세월에 닳아버린 비문을 손으로 더듬었습니다. 그 상징들은 입 밖으로 내어서는 안 될 것들과 종족 전체의 존재를 대가로 치러야 했던 깨달음에 대해 속삭입니다.

하지만 다른 이들이 위험을 볼 때, 나는 의무를 봅니다. 우리 고대 유물부는 알려져서는 안 될 것들의 관리자입니다. 우리의 짐은 보존의 짐입니다. 그런 지식을 낭비하고 오용할 대중을 위해서가 아니라, 그것을 휘두를 지혜를 가진 자들을 위해서 말입니다.

[베리스 하이단의 코덱스 제1권은 제국 학자들 사이에서 널리 유통되었으나 일반적인 접근은 제한되었습니다. 학식 있는 자들 사이에서도 제국이 발견되지 않는 편이 낫다고 판단하는 것들이 있습니다.]

locations.vanilla_source_en:
A Gathering of Starlight to a Greater End

By Keeper Aquilus of the "Sanctum Universum"

Volume 1

Put again from your mind any notion of what you might have once learned about something people call God. Have no assumptions about belief or even divinity itself. If you are a believer by natural aptitude, try and place yourself in the mindset of the pure empiricist who adheres to the strictest scientism. If you are not a believer, take your skepticism and elevate it to its highest orders such that you will not even admit the smallest sense of the spiritual, the superstitious, or even such thing as a lucky roll of the dice.

All is physical, and all is determined. What we don't understand is simply for lack of exploration or appropriate mathematical tools. With sophisticated enough observatory instruments, we could explain the movements of every particle of being from the subatomic to the supercluster. There is no unseen hand which created anything, simply the forces of physics working mindlessly at each other.

And yet, a sunset may be still be lovely.

Certainly, we may be able to pinpoint the exact chemical breakdown of an atmosphere that refracts light from certain star types in a way that the human visual system finds pleasing, but this knowledge does not reduce the beauty... it rather enhances it. We may say that notions of beauty vary across societies and ages, but even such relativism cannot rob us of our particular experience in a given moment. We may not wish to see ourselves as anything more than happenstance firings of chemical signals driven by the grim lurchings of evolutionary processes, but to reduce ourselves thus still leaves the reality of a mind existing at a specific instant to experience a certain pattern of photons that it interprets in a manner that it finds beneficial in some way.

I would hope, even if you admit no possibility of the supernatural, that there is still space in your worldview for awe and for wonder. The universe is charged with grandeur. When we experience that grandeur, we come closer to the underlying reality of the universe.

items.source_en:
From: Dr. Sandra Ram
Subject: Project Archangel
Date: 5 Selona, 7968 C.RC

Hey, I'm sorry to hear about the suspension of Project XNN. It was bold and ambitious, as all your work is! But since you're now free, I was wondering if you might consider bringing that big, bold way of thinking to our project instead?

I know the team has been trying to design a ship that will take full advantage of our pilots' flying prowess. And with the recent accidents, we could all use a pick me up. That's why I've drawn up this supplementary proposal to alter the engine and the fuel of the latest prototype.

Historically, we've sought lighter elements. Hydrogen as a property is 57 times lighter than gaseous vapors, and 14 times lighter than air! It's odorless, and non-corrosive. Liquid hydrogen, combined with oxidizers, was basically the go to fuel in old school space exploration.

And yeah, more modern engines have done the opposite, going with the weightier, gravitational warping to bend space-time. So we made the switch from Hydrogen fuel to Helium, which is also way less flammable and requires less venting. It's the preferred choice in powering hyperdrives.

Now, I've always been a contrarian -- mom always said so, anyway, so maybe this is all just foolish speculation. But I wonder if a shift back to hydrogen based fuel may be worth exploring? Given the crystallization process on other planets can enrich chemical properties in different ways and reduce hydrogen's more volatile tendencies, maybe we need to explore the possibilities of a hydrogen based hyperdrive? 

I don't know, just a thought, but one that's been rattling around in my brain for a hot minute now. So after I dot my i's and cross my t's, I'm thinking of pitching the idea to Dr. Vogel next week, but I would love to hear your feedback on the idea first.
items.legacy_ko:
발신: 산드라 람 박사
제목: 아크엔젤 프로젝트
날짜: 7968년 셀로나 5일

안녕하세요, XNN 프로젝트가 중단되었다는 소식을 듣고 유감스러웠습니다. 당신의 모든 연구가 그렇듯 대담하고 야심 찬 프로젝트였는데 말이죠! 하지만 이제 시간이 좀 나실 테니, 그 크고 대담한 사고방식을 우리 프로젝트에 적용해보는 건 어떨까 해서 연락 드립니다.

우리 팀은 조종사들의 비행 능력을 최대한 활용할 수 있는 함선을 설계하려고 노력 중입니다. 최근 사고들도 있었으니, 우리 모두 기분 전환이 좀 필요하기도 하고요. 그래서 최신 프로토타입의 엔진과 연료를 변경하기 위한 보충 제안서를 작성해봤습니다.

역사적으로 우리는 더 가벼운 원소를 찾아왔습니다. 수소는 기체 증기보다 57배, 공기보다 14배나 가볍습니다! 냄새도 없고 부식성도 없죠. 액체 수소는 산화제와 결합하여 과거 우주 탐사에서 기본 연료로 사용되었습니다.

물론 더 현대적인 엔진들은 정반대의 방식을 택해, 더 무거운 중력 왜곡을 이용해 시공간을 휘게 만들었죠. 그래서 우리는 수소 연료에서 헬륨으로 전환했는데, 헬륨은 훨씬 덜 가연성이고 배출도 덜 필요합니다. 하이퍼드라이브 동력원으로 선호되는 방식이죠.

저는 항상 남들과 다른 생각을 하는 편이라, 어머니도 늘 그렇게 말씀하셨죠. 그래서 이게 다 부질없는 추측일지도 모릅니다. 하지만 수소 기반 연료로 다시 돌아가는 것을 고려해볼 가치가 있지 않을까요? 다른 행성의 결정화 과정이 화학적 특성을 다르게 강화하고 수소의 휘발성을 줄일 수 있다는 점을 고려하면, 수소 기반 하이퍼드라이브의 가능성을 탐구해볼 필요가 있지 않을까요?

잘 모르겠습니다. 그냥 생각일 뿐이지만, 한참 동안 머릿속을 맴돌던 아이디어라 말이죠. 꼼꼼히 검토해본 뒤 다음 주에 보겔 박사님께 제안해볼 생각인데, 그전에 당신의 의견을 먼저 들어보고 싶습니다.

잘 모르겠습니다. 그냥 생각일 뿐이지만, 한참 동안 머릿속을 맴돌던 아이디어라 말이죠. 꼼꼼히 검토해본 뒤 다음 주에 보겔 박사님께 제안해볼 생각인데, 그전에 당신의 의견을 먼저 들어보고 싶습니다.

locations.vanilla_source_en:
From: Dr. Sandra Ram
Subject: Project Archangel
Date: 03/05/2330

Hey, I'm sorry to hear about the suspension of Project XNN. It was bold and ambitious, as all your work is! But since you're now free, I was wondering if you might consider bringing that big, bold way of thinking to our project instead?

I know the team has been trying to design a ship that will take full advantage of our pilots' flying prowess. And with the recent accidents, we could all use a pick me up. That's why I've drawn up this supplementary proposal to alter the engine and the fuel of the latest prototype.

Historically, we've sought lighter elements. Hydrogen as a property is 57 times lighter than gaseous vapors, and 14 times lighter than air! It's odorless, and non-corrosive. Liquid hydrogen, combined with oxidizers, was basically the go to fuel in old school space exploration.

And yeah, more modern engines have done the opposite, going with the weightier, gravitational warping to bend space-time. So we made the switch from Hydrogen fuel to Helium, which is also way less flammable and requires less venting. It's the preferred choice in powering grav drives.

Now, I've always been a contrarian -- mom always said so, anyway, so maybe this is all just foolish speculation. But I wonder if a shift back to hydrogen based fuel may be worth exploring? Given the crystallization process on other planets can enrich chemical properties in different ways and reduce hydrogen's more volatile tendencies, maybe we need to explore the possibilities of a hydrogen based grav drive? 

I don't know, just a thought, but one that's been rattling around in my brain for a hot minute now. So after I dot my i's and cross my t's, I'm thinking of pitching the idea to Dr. Vogel next week, but I would love to hear your feedback on the idea first.

items.source_en:
It's no secret that we've had trouble explaining to the officials at MAST the urgency of the Shadow Collective menace. Despite the fact that they are a disorganized band of pirates, they must be treated as a criminal organization that poses a threat to the safety of the Galaxy.

Unfortunately, without intel on the inner workings of the Shadow Collective, much of this is speculation. We need someone on the inside to help us fill in the blanks. This is why I've requested the records of every prisoner detained by the Galactic Empire. Surely there is a candidate among them who will suit our needs.

items.source_en:
Frost creeps along the visor, obscuring the face beneath, but you can still make out the eerie stillness of death.

A faint crack in the chestplate tells a story of sudden decompression. The emergency seals never engaged. A desperate final attempt to patch the breach is evident. Sealant foam frozen in mid-expansion, an unfinished fix that came seconds too late.

Their mission log, still flickering on a nearby wrist module, simply reads: 

Running out of time. If anyone finds this… 

The message cuts off. They never got to finish it.
items.legacy_ko:
바이저를 따라 서리가 내려앉아 얼굴을 가리고 있지만, 죽음의 기괴한 정적은 여전히 느껴집니다.

흉갑에 난 희미한 균열은 급격한 감압이 일어났음을 말해줍니다. 비상 밀폐 장치는 작동하지 않았습니다. 파손 부위를 막으려던 필사적인 마지막 시도가 보입니다. 팽창하다 얼어붙은 밀폐용 폼은, 몇 초 늦게 도착한 미완의 수리 흔적입니다.

근처 손목 모듈에서 여전히 깜빡이는 임무 기록에는 이렇게 적혀 있습니다.

시간이 다 됐어. 이걸 발견하는 사람이 있다면…

메시지는 거기서 끊겨 있습니다. 끝내 다 적지 못한 모양입니다.
